question: Will Cleitinho Azevedo win the 2026 Minas Gerais gubernatorial election?
rules:
The Minas Gerais gubernatorial election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026, with a runoff on October 25, 2026, if no candidate receives a majority of the valid votes in the first round.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder governors appointed by any means before the specified election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., www.tse.jus.br/eleicoes/resultados-eleicoes).

evidence.excerpt: A Real Time Big Data poll published September 21 put Cleitinho at 35% in the first round, followed by Patrus Ananias at 19%, Alexandre Kalil at 10% and Mateus Simões at 10%. In a simulated runoff, Cleitinho had 43% against Patrus's 42%, a technical tie within the two-percentage-point margin of error. Cleitinho led Kalil 46%–35% and Simões 44%–37% in the other runoff scenarios. The institute interviewed 2,000 voters September 16–19 using telephone interviews and digital recruitment, with 95% confidence and TSE registration MG-07331/2026.

An Itatiaia/Ver poll released September 21 showed Cleitinho with 42.8% of first-round voting intentions, Patrus Ananias with 15.7%, Alexandre Kalil with 9.3% and Mateus Simões with 6.3%. Undecided voters accounted for 14%, while blank or null voting intentions totaled 4.8%. The poll interviewed 1,197 voters and reported a margin of error of 2.8 percentage points at 95% confidence, under TSE registration MG-07337/2026.

A Veritá poll reported Cleitinho with 47.4% of first-round voting intentions and Patrus Ananias with 21.2%. The institute interviewed 2,030 voters September 12–17 using an automated response system with voice recognition and audio-to-text transcription. The reported margin of error was 2.5 percentage points; the survey was registered with the TSE under MG-05919/2026 and BR-03240/2026.

Datafolha reported Cleitinho leading with 37%, compared with 32% in August, followed by Patrus Ananias at 13% and Alexandre Kalil at 11%. Blank or null voting intentions were 11%, and undecided voters were 10%. Excluding blank, null and undecided responses, Cleitinho had 47% of valid voting intentions. Datafolha conducted 1,204 in-person interviews in 55 municipalities September 8–10, with a three-percentage-point margin of error at 95% confidence and TSE registrations MG-01611/2026 and BR-03022/2026.

A Quaest poll put Cleitinho at 32%, up from 29% in August, with Patrus Ananias and Alexandre Kalil at 11% each and Mateus Simões at 8%. Undecided voters totaled 19%, while 12% intended to vote blank or null or not vote. The Globo-commissioned survey interviewed 1,506 voters September 4–7, with a three-percentage-point margin of error at 95% confidence and TSE registration MG-04716/2026. The report also described the PL fielding Flávio Roscoe after uncertainty over Cleitinho's candidacy, while Cleitinho maintained support for Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy.

evidence.publisher: Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Santa Catarina (TRE-SC)
evidence.excerpt: Brazil's 2026 general elections were scheduled for October 4, including voting for state governors. Any second round was scheduled for October 25. The electoral calendar provided for party conventions July 20–August 5, candidate registration by August 15 and the start of electoral campaigning August 16.
